approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted observations in the current task. It retains the best 64 molecules for breeding, draws parents from weighted high-score quantiles, and builds fresh pools through fragment crossover and ordinary multistep atom, bond and ring mutations. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange stays disabled. Stable molecular identities and duplicate rejection precede a source-relative sulfur admission rule: a candidate cannot introduce more of an outside-envelope local sulfur signature than the maximum already present in its original scored generating parents. A Gaussian process fits the complete chronological accepted archive using folded integer Morgan environment counts and dot-product count Tanimoto covariance. It uses the archive's raw-score mean and population standard deviation, fixed noise, and correlated function draws to select ten distinct members of each fresh 160-member pool. Accepted results immediately update breeding survivors and later posterior fits.
approach.novelty: Use the exact fixed exponential warp of count Tanimoto as one coherent Gaussian process for both predicted means and conditional residuals. The two current sibling experiments replaced only the mean or only the residual and both lost endpoint score; this registered joint treatment tests their missing coherent combination while preserving sulfur admission and the rest of the Parent. The older complete exponential experiment used an ungated breeder and cannot supply this current treatment. This test may show another loss: any apparent improvement in prediction or new cores must also reach stronger actual offspring, incumbent progress and the complete endpoint panel. The four current laws can then support a descriptive interaction contrast with their shared control and adaptive histories retained.

observed_bottleneck: The current sulfur-gated Parent n-1744a1494180 still couples count-Tanimoto predicted quality with correlated exploration without delivering reliable absolute progress: its complete mean is 0.59645311428869, population SD 0.03397032998399878, and its sulfur-only gain over n-62daf219c70a is just +0.0007834645552323346 with one losing seed. It has 648 strict generating-parent beats but only 255 sequential incumbent advances among 4350 evaluated offspring, with mean offspring 0.372049560842182 versus best-generating-parent 0.4553040448335957. Both current isolated exponential outputs execute but lose endpoints: n-14a52e3f8725 (E mean/original residual) loses 0.058268979310065 and all seed macros despite better selected-label ranking/MSE; n-6ebafca203bf (original mean/E residual) loses 0.029710059812609 despite seven positive endpoints, a positive seed, and productive-core increases. Their different favorable cells leave the current coherent joint law unmeasured. The older fullE n-07dd356cb779 loses 0.032277693549492024 against ungated n-62daf219c70a, including a positive seed and six positive endpoints; that is an adverse conditional precedent, not the missing current treatment. The limitation tested is whether coherent prediction and exploration geometry can improve absolute source/offspring/incumbent quality where the isolated output routes did not; a covariance-floor or chemical mediator is not identified. Current squared-law n-36a7bb9883ec and allocation-prefix n-605c7a785b51 also lose endpoints despite some attractive ranking/core proxies, reinforcing that activation or novelty alone is insufficient.
hypothesis: Replace the original dot-product count-Tanimoto GP law on sulfur-gated Parent n-1744a1494180 by the fixed coherent K_E(x,y)=exp(T_DP(x,y)-1), lambda=1, in every active training/training, training/query and query/query Gram block, so both active predictive mean mu_E and conditional residual covariance C_E come from that same exponential GP; preserve the original correlated sampling, masks and all other mechanisms.

finding_summary.headline: Coherent exponential GP ran exactly and made choices more local, but lost 0.0332 against the Parent; the full exponential route ends
finding_summary.insights:
The fixed exponential warp is now settled as an endpoint route on this Parent. The mean-only, residual-only and coherent versions all lose between 0.030 and 0.058, as the older ungated full law did, and the registered one-test rule ends this recipe. Coherence did not rescue the hybrids: it cut the mean-only hybrid's loss but landed no better than the residual-only hybrid. The positive four-law interaction is not synergy. It mostly reflects that all three exponential variants reach similar endpoints and miss the same rare Parent discoveries, for example 0.61 to 0.62 against the Parent's 0.856 on deco-hop seed 0, so their losses do not add up.

The run also shows how the warp acts on allocation. Its constant exp(-1) floor ties every candidate to the whole archive. That is consistent with what was measured: the displaced distant candidates lost predicted mean (0.071 lower than under the original law) and some uncertainty, so the law drops far, small, uncertain molecules and samples near what is already known. Its choices track the mean-only hybrid (90% shared) much more closely than the residual-only hybrid (76%), so the mean path drives most of the change. This is the opposite of the broader productive exploration the research brief asks for. The result was more and smaller local wins, a higher offspring average, and less total incumbent progress. It is also one more counterexample showing that better prediction on the selected stream does not carry through to endpoints.

Whether locality causes the loss is still open, and the evidence argues against a simple story: the Parent's largest late jump (deco-hop seed 0, +0.247) was itself a near edit, and the Child gained more than the Parent from distant moves. Locality is a measured signature here, not an identified mediator. The Molecular assessment explains part of the deco-hop gap: this node never built the fused 6-6 diazine bicycle behind the Parent's 0.856. It also identifies chemistry problems that no covariance choice touches: leaders built on N- and O-halogen artefacts, single-atom decoration only, and unbounded molecular size. Worth testing next are allocation rules that preserve or reward uncertainty about distant candidates instead of shrinking it, and generator-side changes such as balanced growth and deletion, fragment-level substitutions and ring annulation, which a kernel change cannot supply.
finding_summary.results:
All 15 task/seed runs completed with 300 observations each. The exponential covariance was used in every training, cross and pool block of all 435 decision pools, and both of its outputs moved in every pool. Compared with the original law recomputed on the same archive, pool and random draws, predicted means shifted by up to 0.55 (0.016 on average, and lower on average in every pool), conditional variances shifted by up to 0.30, and every pool mean and covariance entry changed. The original law would have picked a different set of ten in 417 of 435 pools, and 1,260 of the 4,350 evaluated offspring (29%) were choices it would not have made. Those choices were systematically more local. On identical pools, the exponential law's picks sat at a mean nearest-archive distance of 0.095, versus 0.182 for the original law's picks, with lower uncertainty and slightly larger molecules (35.3 versus 32.6 heavy atoms). The 1,260 candidates it displaced were distant (0.383), small (25 heavy atoms) and uncertain.

On the molecules actually evaluated, the exponential means predicted the real labels slightly better than the original law would have on the same molecules: MSE 0.00790 versus 0.00860, pair-order accuracy 66.8% versus 66.3%, and mean batch Spearman 0.431 versus 0.420. Pair ordering was nevertheless worse on all three deco-hop seeds. Against the Parent's own run, offspring scored higher on average (0.400 versus 0.372), strict wins over the best generating parent rose from 648 to 703, wins carrying a new scaffold rose from 262 to 340, and productive descendant edges rose from 780 to 854. But the wins were smaller (mean gain over the parent 0.0187 versus 0.0266), and total incumbent progress fell from 5.82 to 5.32 summed over the 15 runs, mostly on deco-hop and sitagliptin.

The final macro score was 0.5633 against the Parent's 0.5965, a paired change of -0.0332 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were -0.081, +0.007 and -0.025. Eight of 15 task/seed endpoints improved and seven worsened, with the losses concentrated in deco-hop seed 0 (-0.236), sitagliptin seed 0 (-0.192) and sitagliptin seed 2 (-0.094). Seed-to-seed spread narrowed sharply (population SD 0.0052 versus 0.0340), but around a lower mean. Among the four current laws, the full exponential law (0.5633) sits between the residual-only hybrid (0.5667) and the mean-only hybrid (0.5382), and all three are below the original (0.5965). The descriptive four-law interaction is +0.055, positive in 10 of 15 cells. In one deco-hop seed the selected molecules grew to the 120-atom cap, and that task took 4,635 s of its 7,200 s limit.

molecular.headline: Flat halogen-decorated aromatics from single-atom edits; leaders on two objectives are N- and O-halogenated compounds no chemist could make
molecular.overall_character: Across all 4350 optimizer proposals (870 per objective, three Search Seeds) the generator emits small-to-medium, fully flat, heavily halogenated aromatic heterocycles. Rings and aromatic atoms are essentially universal (digest ring_closure_rate 0.9954-1.0, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9943-1.0), but that ring content is almost entirely inherited from the ten initial molecules and then shuffled: new rings appear mostly as biaryl links (844/870 of one objective's proposals carry a '-c' biaryl bond) rather than as newly built fused bicycles. The chemistry is uniformly neutral and achiral - 0/4350 proposals carry a formal charge and 0/4350 carry a stereobond, matching the digest charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0 on every objective. The decoration vocabulary is almost entirely single atoms: 0/4350 contain a trifluoromethyl group, 6/4350 contain a gem-disubstituted carbon C(C)(C), and the only sulfonyl groups in the whole run (124/4350) are the inherited initial sulfonamide, which disappears by evaluation 70 at the latest and is never re-introduced. What the optimizer does instead is permute F, Cl and Br and attach them to heteroatoms: N-F, N-Cl, N-Br, O-F, O-Cl, O-O, N-N and N-O bonds appear in 48%, 35%, 27%, 12% and 10% of proposals on the five objectives, and in 24/30 of the top-scoring molecules on one of them. Search is strongly local - 49-77% of proposals sit within edit distance 3 of an earlier proposal in the same seed and objective - so each seed converges onto one decorated scaffold and much of the budget buys exactly tied scores.

per_task.generated_character: Compact molecules, mean SMILES length 44.4 and maximum 63, all built on one inherited bicyclic core: the initial 5-methoxy-indole-2-carboxanilide 'COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC' at 0.305 is redecorated for 290 evaluations into methoxy/methyl indole and N-aminopyrrole carboxamides. Every one of the three top molecules is the same scaffold with halogens permuted. There is no stereochemistry and no formal charge anywhere (digest stereocentre_rate and charged_rate both 0.0), and 73.7% of proposals carry a halogen.
liabilities: N-halogenated amides dominate the leaders: 24 of the top 30 molecules carry an N(F), N(Cl) or N(Br) amide nitrogen, which is a reagent-grade halogenating agent, not a compound
benzylic halides CH2F/CH2Cl/CH2Br on the aromatic core of nearly every leader, e.g. 'CC1=Cc2[nH]c(C(=O)C(=O)N(F)c3ccccc3)cc2NC(C)=C1CCl', are hard alkylators
N-hydroxy / N-O pyrrole nitrogens in the final molecules, e.g. 'Cc1c(CBr)cc2c(cc(C(=O)c3cccc(C=N)c3)n2O)c1C'
free aryl imines (C=N, 303/870 proposals) that would hydrolyse on isolation
peroxide O-O fragments reach the oracle at all (13/870), including the zero-scoring 'OO'
missing_features: no nitrile at all in the winning series (C#N appears in 2/870 proposals, best 0.3775), so the aryl-cyano group the leaders would need is never tried
no N-alkyl acetamide: the N-C(C)=O motif occurs in 0/870 proposals
no fused pyrazolo-fused diazine bicycle; only 2/870 proposals contain an n-n ring bond at all
no way to swap the inherited indole core for a different fused heteroaromatic - every top molecule is a decoration of the one initial bicycle
halogen-free decoration: 73.7% of proposals carry a halogen and the whole leader series is halogenated, so unhalogenated analogues are barely sampled
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score climbs from 0.0 for fragments like 'OO' and 'Cl' to 0.461 purely by hanging more substituents on the inherited indole-2-carboxamide: proposals carrying an aryl carboxamide average 0.340 against 0.314 without, and those carrying a fused [nH] bicycle average 0.341 against 0.308. Beyond that the surface is flat and the optimizer exploits the flatness - 'COc1c(CF)c(C)cc2c1cc(C(=O)N(F)c1ccccc1)n2N', its N-Br analogue and its CH2Br/N-Br analogue all return the bit-identical score 0.46092619585962435, and the top 87 molecules span only 39 distinct score values.

per_task.generated_character: By far the largest molecules in the run and the only ones that grow without limit: mean SMILES length 107.9 against 44-58 on the other four objectives, maximum 220, and 325 of 870 proposals longer than 100 characters. Seed 2 inflates monotonically - block means of 71, 130, 194, 210 and 209 characters over the 290 optimizer proposals - and ends on 204-213 character polyaryl assemblies such as the evaluation-300 molecule, which strings together four pyridines, a phenyl, a caffeine-like xanthine and two N-methylurea-pyrazoles. Seed 1 stays compact and finds the best molecule. Xanthine fragments inherited from the initial pool persist in 409/870 proposals and 88.4% of proposals carry a halogen.
liabilities: hypochlorite-type O-Cl groups in 259/870 proposals and in 11 of the top 30, e.g. the leader 'CSC(=CC(C)F)c1c(-c2cncc(-c3cnc(-c4cnc(F)c(Cl)c4CCl)nc3CCF)c2C)nc(=O)oc1C=COCCl'
chloromethyl groups in 200/870 proposals, directly on electron-poor pyridines where they are potent alkylators
the seed-2 endgame molecules of 204-213 characters are far outside any oral drug space and would not be made
vinyl thioethers and enol ethers conjugated into oxazinone rings in the leaders, which are hydrolytically fragile
allene C=C= fragments in 15/870 proposals and peroxides in 24/870
missing_features: fused quinazoline-type 6-6 diazine ring: only 26/870 proposals contain one and none of them lead
the generator links rings instead of fusing them - 844/870 proposals carry a biaryl '-c' bond
no compact high-scoring scaffold at all; the whole run sits in a 0.5 to 0.624 band
no aryl ether on the fused bicycle, the decoration the leading series would require
no sulfonamide anywhere (0/870), so that class of linker is never explored
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The objective pays 0.5 for almost anything - the single-bond fragment 'CF' scores exactly 0.5 - so the whole run occupies a 0.5 to 0.624 band and the gradient above the floor is small and easily faked by size. Length buys nothing: proposals over 120 characters average 0.591 against 0.592 for shorter ones, while seed 2 tripled its molecular size and finished at 0.596. The real signal is a specific fused 6-6 diazine the generator barely makes: only 26/870 proposals contain a fused 'ncnc' bicycle and the best of those reaches 0.5965, whereas the published Parent reached 0.8561 on molecules that all contain one. This node never built that ring.

per_task.generated_character: The most medicinally recognisable chemistry in the run and the only objective the node effectively solves (best 0.9999996). The leaders are 4-aryl-piperidines bearing a basic ring nitrogen alkylated with a 1-aryl-2-aminoethyl arm, e.g. 'COc1cccc(C2CCN(C(CN)C(Cl)c3cc(Cl)cc(Br)c3)CC2)c1C': an anisole, a saturated basic amine and a polyhalogenated aryl. Halogens are near-universal (digest halogen_rate 0.9943) and the top 30 average two chlorines and one bromine. Seed 2 ends somewhere quite different, on strained spiro and bridged aziridine/azetidine polycycles (52/870 proposals contain a three- or four-membered N ring) carrying sulfinyl groups (204/870).
liabilities: every one of the top 30 molecules carries a benzylic chloride C(Cl)c, an electrophile that would alkylate anything before it reached an assay
hypochlorite O-Cl groups in 80/870 proposals and chloramine N-Cl in 33/870, both present in the seed-2 endgame molecules
strained fused aziridine/azetidine polycycles in the final molecules, e.g. 'O=S(CN1CC1CCCN1CC1CN1CCC2CC1c1c(OCl)cc(F)cc12)c1cccc(Cl)c1', which are not credible ring systems
a free primary amine next to a benzylic halide, which would cyclise or self-alkylate immediately
three halogens on one small aryl ring in essentially every leader, pushing lipophilicity well past a sensible range
missing_features: no arylpiperazine at all: 0/870 proposals carry a piperazine N directly on an aromatic ring, the single most common motif in this receptor class
no amide or sulfonamide linker between the amine and the aryl - C(=O)N appears in only 6/870 proposals
no trifluoromethyl or other metabolically blocking group: 0/870
no basic nitrogen presented as its protonated or salt form (digest charged_rate 0.0), although the series is clearly amine-driven
no stereochemistry on the benzylic and piperidine centres the leaders create (digest stereocentre_rate 0.0)
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient is sharp and reads as a clean pharmacophore signal. Proposals with an amine-like nitrogen average 0.694 against 0.042 without; proposals carrying a sulfonyl average 0.059 against 0.788 without; proposals carrying a carboxylic acid average 0.035 and never exceed 0.079. The inherited sulfonylpyrrolidine seeds are the worst molecules in the task ('COS(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1' at 0.000247) and the optimizer deletes that group within 70 evaluations. Progress is therefore: strip the acidic/sulfonyl head, keep a basic amine, add a lipophilic halogenated aryl.

per_task.generated_character: The cleanest and most makeable chemistry of the five, and the lowest-scoring: best 0.2397 over a 0.0183 to 0.2397 span. Mean SMILES length 55.1, halogen_rate only 0.1816, ring_closure_rate 1.0. The leaders are a single hybrid scaffold repeated with small edits - a propyl-azaheteroarene fused through a naphthalene-like tricycle to an ethoxy-pyrrole and a methylated diketopiperazine, e.g. 'CCCc1nn(C)c2[nH]c(OCC)c3c(cc4ccccc4c12)C(=O)N(C)C(=O)CN3C'. Seed 2 ends on a simpler 2-propylquinoline bearing a saturated diketopiperazine ring. These are the only molecules in the run a chemist would call ordinary.
liabilities: N-N hydrazide and N-O hydroxylamine linkages in the seed-2 final molecules, e.g. 'CCCc1cc(N2CCNN3C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C2CC3CC)c2ccccc2n1' and 'CCCc1cc(ON2C3=C4CN(C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C42)N(N)C3)c2ccccc2n1'
an aminal/N-N bridged bicyclic diketopiperazine that would not survive synthesis
peroxide fragments in 17/870 proposals
the top scaffolds are highly fused and planar with no sp3 exit vector, which is a liability for a real series even though each atom is reasonable
missing_features: no sulfonamide anywhere (0/870), so an entire half of the required pharmacophore is never attempted
methylenedioxy-phenyl appears in only 3/870 proposals
piperazine appears in 48/870 and never on a sulfur linker
no fused pyrazolo-pyrimidinone: the generator cannot assemble that bicycle from its single-atom moves
no way to grow a second distinct ring system onto the core - the leaders are all one fused tricycle plus decorations
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Three inherited fragments each pay, and the optimizer simply accumulates all three. Proposals with a propylquinoline average 0.215 against 0.189 without; with an ethoxy OCC 0.213 against 0.191; with an N-methyl diketopiperazine 0.213 against 0.194. Of the top 30, 29 carry the ethoxy and 30 carry an [nH] ring. The low ceiling is the point: 0.2397 against a 0.0183 floor means the objective is rewarding partial resemblance to something the generator can only half-build, and the last 150 evaluations move the best score by under 0.006.

per_task.generated_character: The widest score span in the run (6.3e-48 to 0.5438) and the most contorted molecules. The leaders are dense polyfused cages - pyrimidinone/imidazole ring systems closed through four or five ring-closure digits onto a fluorinated cyclobutene and a lactone, e.g. 'CCC1c2c3c(=N)n(C(F)CF)c(=O)n4c3cn2C2(F)C(=CC2F)OC1C4=O'. The second family, from seed 2, is a biaryl-linked xanthine bearing an acyl fluoride and fluoromethyl groups. Fluorine is the whole currency: the top 30 average 3.2 fluorines, 374/870 proposals carry three or more, and 71/870 carry a CHF2 group.
liabilities: acyl fluorides in 127/870 proposals including the whole seed-2 leader family, e.g. 'Cc1c(C(=O)F)c2cc(c1-n1c(CF)c3c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n(C)c3c1F)CN2'; these acylate water on contact
N-fluoro imide nitrogens in the final molecules, e.g. 'Cc1c(C(=O)F)c2cc(c1-n1cc3c(c1CF)c(=O)n(F)c(=O)n3F)CCN2'
fluoromethyl and chloromethyl groups on heteroaromatic nitrogen, which are alkylating
bridged tetracyclic cages with two adjacent quaternary ring-fusion carbons and an enol lactone, for which no synthesis is obvious
cumulated double bonds in 2.6% of proposals (digest cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.0264) and terminal alkynes in 50/870
missing_features: trifluoromethyl group: 0/870 here and 0/4350 across the whole node, although fluorine count is the clearest thing the score rewards
a polyfluorinated benzene ring - the leaders put fluorine on sp3 carbons and ring nitrogens instead
beta-amino amide: a free primary amine appears in only 8/870 proposals and the best of those scores 0.0309
triazole or other fused 5-6 N3 heterocycle: 2/870 proposals
any stereochemistry at all (digest stereocentre_rate 0.0) on molecules with four or five sp3 ring-fusion carbons
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Fluorine count is the single visible driver: proposals with three or more fluorines average 0.282 and reach 0.544, those with fewer average 0.137. The inherited xanthine dimers are the catastrophic losers (6.3e-48 and 1.7e-47), and even bare 'CC' scores 8.8e-21, so the objective punishes the starting pool hard and rewards compact fluorinated heterocycles. But fluorine is added one atom at a time - a CF3 group never appears in any of the 4350 proposals in this node - so the series saturates around 0.54 by decorating a cage rather than by building the substituent pattern the gradient is pointing at.

transferable_gaps.evidence: N-F, N-Cl, N-Br, O-F, O-Cl, O-O, N-N and N-O bonds appear in 48%, 35%, 27%, 12% and 10% of the optimizer proposals on the five objectives. They are not confined to the failures: on one objective 24 of the top 30 molecules carry an N-halogen amide, and three molecules that differ only by swapping N-F for N-Br and CH2F for CH2Br return the bit-identical score 0.46092619585962435. On another, 11 of the top 30 carry an O-Cl hypochlorite ester. These bonds are what a reagent is made of, not a compound.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator forms bonds between heteroatoms and halogens, and between heteroatoms and each other, as freely as it forms carbon-heteroatom bonds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Candidate construction needs a valence-context rule, not just a valence count: a halogen may attach to carbon but not to N, O or S, and N-N, N-O and O-O single bonds should only be formed inside recognised ring or functional contexts. Because the score surface does not penalise these bonds, filtering them has to happen in the proposal operator rather than being left to selection, and the operator should offer a carbon-attached alternative in their place so the edit is not simply lost.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across all 4350 optimizer proposals in this node there are 0 trifluoromethyl groups, 6 gem-disubstituted carbons of the form C(C)(C), and 0 sulfonamides introduced de novo - the only 124 sulfonyl-bearing proposals all descend from one inherited starting molecule and the last of them is evaluation 70. On the objective where fluorine count is the clearest thing the score rewards (three-or-more-fluorine proposals average 0.282 against 0.137), the generator still never assembles a CF3; it reaches a maximum of CHF2 in 71 proposals and then saturates.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can only decorate with single atoms; it never inserts a multi-atom functional group.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The move set should include whole-fragment substitution from a small library of standard medicinal chemistry groups - trifluoromethyl, sulfonamide, nitrile, carbamate, gem-dimethyl - applied as one atomic edit. A sequence of single-atom edits cannot reach these groups because each intermediate is a worse molecule, so no hill-climber will pay for the path. A fragment-level operator makes the whole group a one-step move whose intermediate penalty never has to be paid.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On one objective the mean SMILES length is 107.9 with a maximum of 220 and 325 of 870 proposals over 100 characters, while the other four objectives sit at 44-58 characters. One seed of that objective grew monotonically through block means of 71, 130, 194, 210 and 209 characters and finished on 204-213 character polyaryl assemblies scoring 0.5958-0.5961, against a best of 0.6235 found by a compact seed. Proposals over 120 characters average 0.591, those under 120 average 0.592: the growth bought nothing.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecule size is unbounded, and at least one run inflated by a factor of three with no score return.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The proposal operator needs a size control that is a property of the generator rather than of the objective - a soft cap on heavy-atom count, a deletion move offered at the same rate as the addition move, or a size term inside candidate acceptance. Note that the run which stayed compact found the best molecule, so the control should bias toward parity between growing and shrinking edits rather than simply truncating.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring content is universal (digest ring_closure_rate 0.9954-1.0) but it is inherited: on one objective 844/870 proposals carry a biaryl '-c' link while only 26/870 contain a fused 6-6 diazine bicycle, and the published code Parent reached 0.8561 on molecules that all contain one while this node's best was 0.6235. On another objective every one of the top twelve molecules is a decoration of the same inherited bicyclic core. Where the generator does close new rings it produces strained three- and four-membered nitrogen rings in bridged polycycles (52/870 on one objective) rather than ordinary fused aromatics.
transferable_gaps.gap: New rings are made by joining existing ring atoms, not by constructing new fused bicyclic systems, so the available scaffolds are whatever the starting pool contained.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The move set needs a ring-construction operator that can annulate a new six-membered aromatic or heteroaromatic ring onto an existing one in a single step, and a ring-replacement operator that can exchange one fused bicycle for another of the same attachment topology. Without those, the reachable scaffold set is the union of what the initial pool supplies, and the search can only redecorate it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 0 of 4350 optimizer proposals carry a stereobond and 0 carry a formal charge, matching the digest stereocentre_rate 0.0 and charged_rate 0.0 on every objective. This is not because the molecules are flat: the leading series on one objective has four or five sp3 ring-fusion carbons, and the leading series on another is driven by an sp3 amine whose proposals average 0.694 against 0.042 for proposals without one. Every molecule reaching the oracle is therefore an unspecified mixture presented as a neutral free base.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits no stereochemistry and no ionisation state, even on molecules whose scoring centres are stereogenic or basic.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generated SMILES should carry explicit configuration wherever an sp3 centre has four distinct substituents, with the operator either preserving the parent configuration through an edit or enumerating both, and should express the dominant protonation state for strongly basic or acidic centres. Tautomer choice should be made explicitly rather than inherited from string position.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 49-77% of optimizer proposals sit within edit distance 3 of an earlier proposal in the same seed and objective. Halogens are nearly universal where they help (halogen_rate 0.9943, 0.8839 and 0.8034 on three objectives) and the leaders differ only in which halogen sits where: on one objective the top 87 molecules span only 39 distinct score values, and three leaders tie at exactly 0.46092619585962435. Each seed converges on a single decorated scaffold and the last 150 evaluations on one objective move the best score by under 0.006.
transferable_gaps.gap: Search is overwhelmingly local and spends a large share of its budget on score-neutral halogen permutations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The operator should treat an edit that only exchanges one halogen for another as a low-information move and down-weight it once a tie has been observed, and candidate selection should require a minimum structural distance from already-evaluated molecules so that budget buys new scaffolds rather than re-measurements of the same one. A per-seed record of which edit types have produced exact score ties is enough to drive this without any knowledge of what is being optimised.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
